To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chondroblastic differentiation in hyaline cartilaginous tissue is characterized by the formation of dense foci in the cell cortex, the development of an extensive endo- plasmic reticu- lum, the concentration of the Golg1 apparatus, the appearance and discharge of membrane-bounded inclusions, and by the elaboration of a matrix of fibrils embedded in an am- orphous ground substance.
the chondroblast is the cell which secretes the cartilage matrix, and that the chondrogenic cells of epiphyseal growth plates are the source of the cells of the bone-forming osteogenic plate.
the chondroblast is the cell of cartilage formation and that the chondrogenic cell fabricates its own matrix by the secretion of fibrils and granules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural changes in the mesenchymal cell which accompany the differentiation of cartilage and the elaboration of the cartilaginous matrix.
the role of the chondrogenic cells in the fabrication and evolution of the cartilage connective tissue matrix.

the following questions: What are the structural modifications of the prechandral mesenchyma and the chondroblast which accompany cytodifferenciation? What are the morphological changes of the chondrogenic cells during their evolution to chondocytes, and what is the role of these cells in the fabrication and maintenance of a connective-tissue matrix?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chondroblast is a highly specialized cell with a complex cytoarchitecture which is capable of elaborating the entire cartilage matrix and that the chondrogenesis is an orderly process of cell differentiation which can be traced in its entirety.

the chondroblast elaborates the cartilage matrix by the secretion of its cytoplasmic constituents, and that this is effected by a process which is basically similar to that which operates in the elaboration of the extracellular matrix by other cell types.
the chondroblast is a cell which secretes the matrix, the chondroctyte is one which disintegrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the matrix of cartilage is a product of the chondrogenic cell.

(1) the chondroblast is the cell of the cartilage, and (2) its differentiation is characterized by the formation of a matrix, and (3) this is accomplished by the secretion of the matrix components from the cytoplasm of chondroblast into the matrix space.

the chondroblast is the matrix-producing cell of hyaline cartilaginous tissue, and that the chondrogenic process is characterized by a progressive specialization of the chondoblast's endoplasmic apparatus and the elaboration of a complex matrix which is the end result of the secretory activity of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cartilage is a highly dynamic tissue, and that the matrix is not a static structure.
the chondroblast is the cell responsible for the formation of the hyaline cartilaginous matrix.
chondrocytic hypertrophy is associated with an increasing capacity for the secretion of matrix material.
